posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I decided I would try to make a Games In Development thread to see if I can take my first real game across the finish line. All concepts, layouts, graphics, features, etc. are works in progress and subject to change. I plan to release this game for FREE on itch.io and maybe Steam (depending on how ugly of a baby it is).
Spoiler:
SYNOPSIS
As the working title suggests, this is a Sudoku inspired game. You might even say it is Sudoku lite or like, given some of the features. At this moment, subject to feedback, suggestions, and sudden bouts of inspiration, here are the main features that are planned:
All Randomly Generated, Solvable Puzzles (Both Pregenerated & On Demand Generation)
Multiple Puzzle Types (Not just Numbers like traditional Sudoku - 12 so far)
Player chooses how many Hints will be initially revealed in the Puzzle (17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 36)
Player chooses either Manual or Auto Hints (Manual means the player chooses where the hints are revealed)
Player chooses either Timer or No Timer
Player chooses either Auto Generated Hints or Pregenerated Hints
Player can insert possible values in squares before making their official choice
Player can change values in the puzzle (but not hints once selected)
Quit Puzzle Option
Save on Demand
Music Selection
Click on Choice and then square to assign a value in the puzzle (No number input)
In game Achievements with Player Hall of Fame area
Two different checks for solved puzzles (Actual solution for Pregenerated puzzles & Valid solution)
Player can elect more Hints if they started with fewer than 36.
Again, all of these features are subject to my ability to incorporate them. Because the puzzles are generated randomly, and the revealed hints can be assigned randomly or by the player, and the number of hints can be selected, and there are more puzzle types than just traditional numbers, there should be excellent replay value.
The Achievements will be designed to encourage the player to explore and try all the different options available.
If the player likes traditional Sudoku, they should be able to make choices that give them an almost unlimited puzzle solving experience. And for those who want a real challenge, they can choose something other than numbers, with less hints that are randomly placed.
Spoiler:
SCREENSHOTS
Tags and Genre for this game would be Puzzle and Sudoku Puzzle.
I welcome any and all feedback and suggestions.
Thanks!
EDIT: UPDATED some information and concepts.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Made pretty good progress so far.
I have 12 working puzzle themes now, I have the Event part that allows the player to select a pre-generated random puzzle (just need to generate and add a bunch more) or a new random puzzle, my random puzzle generator is working without problems (other than being slow sometimes), and I have the Event completed that allows the player to select their own hints based on the total number of hints they selected.
Now comes the part that is probably the hardest. Experimenting and trying to find the best way to auto generate hints. Which is kind of critical for a new, random generated puzzle. With the pre-generated, random puzzles, I can tweak the puzzle hints in advance if I need to.
I also decided to have the Solve Puzzle option do two checks. One will check to see if the puzzle is solved with the exact same values in the exact same places as the puzzle. The other will just check to see if whatever values the player entered results in a valid solution, even if it doesn't match the original puzzle.
This is actually important since I am allowing the player to choose where they place their hints and to select a total number of hints (14) that is lower than what is required (17) for a Sudoku puzzle to have only one valid solution. So getting a solution that "works" even if it isn't a match to the original puzzle is still an "ok" solution.
I have a bunch of ideas to try, but my main concern (probably obvious) is whether or not the methods I use to auto generate the hints will result in visible hints that will allow the player to have clear and obvious selections at the start of the game without having to guess.
I haven't done a TON of Sudoku puzzles and I have mostly stuck with easy or medium puzzles, but I think every one I have done is set up so you can narrow down the value of some squares without having to guess or do the this square could have more than one value thing.
I have to try to see if I can figure out a way to get auto generated hints for a random puzzle that will make sure to give the player a few squares at the start that can only have one value based on the visible puzzle hints based on usual Sudoku puzzle solving strategies.
Now, maybe that won't be possible. But I am certainly going to give it a try by experimenting to see what happens.
I have been researching sample Sudoku puzzles to see if there are any observable patterns to the hint placements and values for the puzzle start.
I have thought about starting with random selection of 1 value for each Group (3x3 grid), then 1 value for each column or row and continuing in that pattern until the hints are exhausted.
I have thought about only selecting values from columns (or rows) to make sure that there are multiple values in most columns.
I have thought about options to make sure that the same value in the puzzle (like say 8) shows up enough times and in the right places to let the player narrow down where another 8 needs to go.
But I am one of those people who has a hard time conceptualizing how things will play out unless I see them in action. So there are limits to how much my theorizing will benefit me.
I guess time will tell. But at least I have ideas of how to start and see what happens when the Event runs.
If anyone has any ideas of how to approach this, besides this isn't possible so don't try, I would be happy to consider them. I am stubborn enough to try anyway, just to see the results. So productive suggestions to achieve that goal are very much appreciated.
But I am still learning a lot while doing this so it is definitely worth it for me.
I hope this update makes sense.
Happy game developing!

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Weekly Progress Update
I spent most of the week puzzling (how punny) over how to Event a new method for Auto Generating Hints that will always result in an Easy puzzle at the maximum hint number of 37. I was researching Sudoku algorithms and while the math is WAY beyond this immortal Zombie's comprehension, I was able to understand the logic of reverse tracking a completed puzzle for determining where to place hints.
Which is what I have been logically trying to organize into an Event. Essentially, you take a completed Sudoku puzzle and remove one square at a time. Each time you remove a square value, you check to see how many possible values could go in that square. If it is only 1, then you still have an Easy puzzle. If it is more than 1, you put the value back and try a different square. You keep doing that until you get to the number of hints remaining you want for the puzzle and you should be left with a puzzle with hints displayed where there is always at least 1 square of the puzzle that has only 1 possible value.
I spent most of my development time this week updating all 81 of the Common Events that are called from the Puzzle squares and the Parallel Event that actually allows the player to complete the puzzle. While it was incredibly tedious work of copying/pasting and changing a bunch of values for each Event for Variables, Switches, Picture Ids, etc., at least all the puzzle squares now have all functionality (designed so far) and seem to work correctly.
So even though I only knocked 1 item off my previous immediate To Do list, I still made good developing progress.
I also inadvertently discovered a serious flaw in the logical design of the majority of the 10 methods of Auto Generating Hints that I Evented. This made Zombie's brain hurt. Essentially, I forgot a very important part that made it so the same square could be picked more than once under certain circumstances for a possible hint. This resulted in random instances of LESS hints than desired. The solution required some experimental testing of the solution logic and then lots of copying/pasting and changing values. But I now have 7 of the 10 correctly updated and functioning now.
I also want to officially extend the offer, like I did in a status post this week, that if anyone has 9 Themed 48x48 pictures that they would like to see as a Puzzle Theme option, I am happy to consider requests since adding Themes is incredibly easy.
@Ziorke
posted an example that looks really cool and they also gave me an idea.
I decided to add two more features.
Try to either add numbers to the Themed images so there is a visual reference for the Note taking mechanic OR add the number references where the player selects the value they want to enter for the square.
Add the option (with detailed instructions) to allow the player to use their own Theme. I will program the Events to accept a generic image name "Custom1-", "Custom2-", and "Custom3-". That way, all the player has to do is place 9 images (48x48) in the appropriate game folder with the exact appropriate file names (like Custom1-1, Custom1-2, Custom1-3, etc.) and they can, in theory, try any images they want in the game for a puzzle Theme. I thought that might be really cool and interesting.
Other than that I also:
Added a couple more Pregenerated puzzles (I am slowly adding up to 30 and will probably increase that as I go)
Added the ability for the player to either choose a specific pregenerated puzzle or do a randomly selected pregenerated puzzle (which means I also now need to add a puzzle identifier to show which pregenerated puzzle is being played)
So this week, my top priorities from the To Do list are:
Finish fixing the existing Auto Generating Hint methods & Test
Event the newest method & Test
Finish the Event for solving the puzzle
And finally, here is a screenshot of a puzzle utilizing the add notes mechanic. As you can see, the player can leave a space in any of the 4 places if they don't have 4 values they want to add.
Spoiler:
Player Added Notes
I hope everyone has a productive week game developing and remember to have fun!

posts.body:
Weekly Progress Update.
I know it probably sounds funny, but I still don't feel...qualified...to call this a Dev Log or to refer to myself as a developer. More like a hobbiest dabbler. Anywho...
I didn't accomplish much this week, but I suppose that is bound to happen once in a while. I ran into a few problems that slowed things down.
First was an unexpected behavior with the ButtonPicture plugin that I heavily rely on for this game. Thankfully, my post on this forum led to a better understanding of what was happening and a very simple solution was offered that I tested successfully.
Second was something that I never did resolve. I had 1 background image, out of 401 that the game wouldn't recognize. I scrutinized it carefully and tried everything I could think of. It didn't seem any different from the other 400 images. And even though the image was the right type and in the right folder, the game just wouldn't show the image in the option for Show Picture. It was the strangest thing. So after hours of fighting with it, I just gave up and selected another image.
So, what did I actually achieve this week? Here it is:
Started implementing the fix to solve the problem with the way I was using the ButtonPicture plugin.
Continued to test different colors to make the semi-transparent Numbers & Letters Puzzle Themes easier to see.
Added the option to also select solid Numbers & Letters.
Added the solid Numbers & Letters examples for the player to preview what they will look like.
Added some new Pregenerated puzzles.
Added Custom Backgrounds & Custom Theme placeholders.
Implemented the functionality for the player to choose a Custom Background or Custom Theme.
I also made a DEMO video about a week ago that I posted on my status feed. I will repost it here as well.
As always, if you have any questions or suggestions, feel free to leave a message or send me a PM.
I hope everyone had a productive week and a Happy Easter!
Happy gaming and Happy game developing!

And although I should have thought of it sooner, I just realized today that I can save the original puzzles that the player generates (if they choose to) and the player can go back to those puzzles just like they would one of the 99 pregenerated puzzles.
I just need to assign the necessary Array variables to store each original puzzle data and then make the functionality to allow the player to see those puzzles as well. So each player would have puzzles that are unique to their game.
I now have 50 of 99 pregenerated puzzles set up in the game.
If you add in the functionality that the player can create their own Themes and Backgrounds, there really isn't a limit to the number of puzzles and variety that the player can experience.

So I actually made pretty good progress in the game for the first time in a while.
I still need to design and develop the Music Menu to expand the Music options, but the limited Music options from the Main Menu are now fully implemented, as follows:
7 categories of BGMs, 1 for each RPG Maker (MZ, MV, VX Ace, VX, XP, 2003, 2000)
447 total BGM files
Option to randomly select a BGM category and BGM file which changes the displayed BGM category name and BGM file number
BGM Fixed option to keep the same BGM playing (On) or BGM changing after X amount of minutes (Off)
When BGM Fixed option is OFF, no other options function because the BGMs are randomly rotating
Option to scroll through the BGM categories (up or down) which changes the displayed BGM category name
Option to randomly select a BGM file within the current BGM category which changes the displayed BGM file number
Option to scroll through the BGM files (up or down) in the current BGM category which changes the displayed BGM file number
BGM Preview Button that stops the current BGM playing and starts a new BGM based on the current BGM category and file number
Option to increase the BGM audio by 5 (up or down)
I also had to make a few changing in the UI appearance of the Main Menu to accommodate longer BGM category names. And the functionality exists to display the BGM file name that looks more normal than the OGG file name.
The Music Menu with have these same options, but will have additional options to make selecting a BGM category or specific BGM file easier and faster as well as setting the amount of time between changes in the BGM when the BGM Fixed option is Off. The Music Menu will have more room for options that couldn't fit on the Main Menu.
I have also decided that with 447 BGM files already for the player to choose from, I won't be adding all of the other free music that I downloaded and converted to OGG files.

posts.body:
Wow! Looking at my last update I can see that my break from this game has been longer than I realized.
I have been focusing on learning Javascript so I can improve the game and make it more efficient.
However, I do have a significant update on one piece that I have been pursuing sporadically.
After many months of trying different things and untold hours of work, I finally had a way of consistently generating a new Sudoku puzzle. And I used that method to generate over 60 puzzles for the game. I was also planning on using it to allow the player to create about 99 original puzzles that they could also save (in addition to the 99 already set up in the game) and then they could generate as many as they wanted after that (they just couldn't save them).
The problem was that the method to generate the puzzle could be as quick as only a few seconds to as long as 4 or more minutes. That was because the method was essentially based on trial and error where if the puzzle generation got to a point it couldn't proceed with a valid puzzle, then the generation process started over.
But after recently trying another method and failing to improve my current method, I was able to test a script that seems to reliably generate a new puzzle in only a few seconds each time. I am still testing it, but it seems to be exponentially better than the method I have been using.
I generated 15 new puzzles in less than a minute.
My next step is testing a script that will take the generated puzzle and reliably turn the necessary number of squares blank for easy, medium, and hard puzzles.
The method I have right now can only reliably make easy puzzles with only one solution.
So, this seems to me to be a significant improvement.
I also made the terrible mistake of starting this game project inside another project that is filled with other unrelated experiments. So, it is a mishmash of things that aren't needed for the game.
So, I need to make a new copy of the project and remove all the unnecessary things that aren't part of the game. When I do that, I also plan on taking the time to reorganize everything and try to improve the coding/scripts to make the entire game more efficient using what I'm learning about JS.
So, I'm working on the game a little at a time while I do other things. Getting a "clean," reorganized, and more efficient project is going to take a significant amount of time.
I hope everyone is doing well! Happy gaming and good luck on your projects!
